title: Variant catalogue: name the 6 variants, front-page gallery, per-variant lab notebook
description: The lab has 3 collision rules x 2 failure rules = 6 playable variants but they are anonymous URL params. (1) Name each variant after its most significant feature. (2) Make index.html a gallery/catalogue that renders from a shared variants.js registry; move the game to play.html (old deep links redirect). (3) Add variants/ docs: one file per variant tracking rules, hypothesis to prove/disprove, feedback log, and branching/extension musings. Update README + AGENTS.md.

title: Isolated failure rule: provisional 'NUMBER NOT UP' semantics
description: Open design question — do NOT quietly settle it. Implement one provisional, isolated rule (candidate: a superposition that does not make Number go UP ends the run) in its own swappable spot next to the collision rule. Candidates from the plan: decrease→death, fail-to-increase→death, invalid result→death, non-numeric/undefined→death, up-undefined-domain→death, something else. On failure: show clearly WHY (which hypothesis of failure fired) so play can judge it. Deep hypothesis being explored: failure is not health-zero, it is NUMBER NOT UP. We don't know yet.
acceptance_criteria: Failure predicate is a single isolated function/binding; changing the death semantics requires no restructuring; the run end states which failure condition fired and offers restart.
close_reason: engine.js FAILURE_RULES isolates the predicate: notUp (provisional: run ends when Number goes DOWN, stays flat, or becomes invalid — reason string states which fired) and none. ?fail= param and F key swap at runtime; run-over screen names the condition and offers R restart. Verified: DOWN/flat/invalid all fail with distinct reasons; none never fails.

title: Isolated collision engine: superpose(current, tile) → result + event record
description: Core operation conceptually: superpose(currentNumber, destinationTile) → result. Must be a tiny isolated module trivially replaceable — no restructuring to try a different interpretation. Ship candidate rules side by side, NOT one 'correct' answer: replacement, addition, operator evaluation (tile operator applies to current Number and... something), and leave room for other interpretations. Rules selectable without code changes where cheap (e.g. ?rule= query param). Record an event per move: {turn, direction, oldNumber, destinationTile, result, delta, wentUp, valid}; keep a cheap run history for comparing rules. Do not assume operators (+ − × ÷) are conventional or that Number+Number must mean arithmetic.
acceptance_criteria: superpose() lives in its own file/section; switching rule interpretation requires changing one binding (or a query param), nothing else; every move appends an event with the listed fields; history is retained in-memory.
close_reason: engine.js isolates superpose(currentNumber, tile, ctx) with three swappable candidate rules (replace/add/eval) plus URL param ?rule= and C key; event record {turn,direction,oldNumber,destinationTile,result,delta,wentUp,valid,failed,failReason} kept in in-memory history. 23 node assertions passed covering all rules, invalid results, and event fields.

title: Movement: dot IS the Number, keyboard input, move is the only verb
description: Player moves through the grid with arrow keys, numpad, and WASD. The dot is not a character on a number — it IS the current Number. Moving into an adjacent cell triggers the superposition event (engine issue handles the rule). Edges block movement (invalid, no event). No interact/attack/collect buttons, no other verbs.
acceptance_criteria: Arrow keys, numpad, and WASD move the dot; edges are blocked; each move into a tile produces a superposition event.
close_reason: Arrows, WASD, and numpad (2/4/6/8) move the dot; edges blocked with feedback; movement is the only verb. Verified via jsdom keypress simulation for all four input families.

title: Scaffold: page shell, three UI regions, SVG 5×5 grid
description: Plain index.html + style.css + script(s), opens directly from file:// (no build, no server, no modules that break file://). Three conceptual regions: (1) status/headline — NUMBER UP + current NUMBER (Number is the score; nothing else), (2) world — SVG 5×5 grid with the hand-authored tiles and the distinct central dot, (3) message/observation area (can start verbose; it's the lab notebook). World data (tiles, start Number) lives in one obvious hand-authored place, trivially editable. Do not add decorative world concepts.
acceptance_criteria: Opening index.html directly shows the 5×5 grid, center dot, current NUMBER 0, and message area.
close_reason: index.html + style.css + SVG grid built: three UI regions (status with NUMBER, world grid with distinct center dot, observation area), world data hand-authored in world.js, opens from file://. Verified via jsdom: grid renders 38 nodes, dot centered at 250,250, NUMBER 0 shown.

title: Number Up MVP — superposition 0 prototype (epic)
description: Runnable local prototype of the Number Up design laboratory (_the_beginning.md). Premise: the player is a central dot and the dot IS the current Number (start 0). Movement is the only verb; moving into a cell is a superposition event whose result must be visible and isolated so rules can be swapped. Plain HTML/CSS/JS + SVG, opens from file://, no framework, no extra primitives (no score/HP/inventory/etc). Success = intrinsic curiosity ('I want to see what happens if I do this'). Deliverable: index.html opens directly; tiny README; then STOP and play.
close_reason: MVP superposition 0 complete: all 8 child issues closed. Prototype runs by opening index.html; engine and DOM verified by 23 node assertions + 33 jsdom checks. Stopping here to play before adding features, per plan.

title: Copy convention: shorthand plus a plain line on gallery cards
description: Adopted convention for variant copy: taglines unchanged (designer shorthand), each gallery card gains one plain mechanics line (how), hypothesis lines rewritten in plain second person. Notebooks untouched. Add VARIANTS.how, render it in gallery.js, restyle cards slightly, update variants/README registry field list.

title: README: run, controls, where rules live; then stop and play
description: Tiny README only: how to run (open index.html), controls, where the collision rule lives, where the failure rule lives, how to change the test world(s). No over-documentation. Explicit note: once it runs, stop and play before adding features.
acceptance_criteria: README covers the five points; nothing else documented; no features added beyond the plan.
close_reason: README.md covers run (open index.html), controls, where collision rule lives (engine.js RULES), where failure rule lives (engine.js FAILURE_RULES), how to change worlds (world.js WORLDS), plus a do-not-add-primitives note and stop-and-play reminder. Nothing over-documented.

title: Four experiment worlds A–D, switchable
description: Hand-authored tiny worlds, selectable via query param/key, no generation: A — Number+Number: numbers only; question: what interaction between two Numbers feels intrinsically interesting? B — Number+Operator: introduce + − × ÷; question: is an operator a thing you collide with or a verb you invoke? C — UP vs DOWN: authored layout where different movement choices give different numeric outcomes; question: does the player start thinking 'how do I make Number go UP'? D — Failure: situations where Number can go down, stay flat, go invalid; exercise the failure semantics; question: does failure feel like a consequence of the premise or a bolted-on rule? World data stays in the one obvious place so worlds are trivially editable.
acceptance_criteria: All four worlds are reachable and playable; switching worlds needs no code edit; each world is a small hand-authored grid in world data.
close_reason: world.js WORLDS: full (mixed), a (numbers only), b (operators), c (UP vs DOWN choices), d (failure situations with ÷0, ×0, flat moves). N key cycles, ?world= param selects; all verified playable in jsdom; no code edits needed to switch.

title: Message/observation area: verbosity levels + debug mode without code changes
description: Lab-notebook message region. Normal mode: concise per-move observation, e.g. 'SUPERPOSITION 0 + 9 → Result: 9. Number went UP: YES'. Debug mode (toggle key or ?debug param — no code changes): verbose detail — move direction, old/new number, delta, tile, rule used, turn index, recent history. Verbosity easy to turn down later.
acceptance_criteria: A toggle switches concise ↔ verbose modes at runtime without editing code; verbose mode shows the event-record fields.
close_reason: Message area shows per-move observation (You moved X / SUPERPOSITION / operands / Result / Number went UP). / key or ?debug=1 toggles verbose mode with full event-record history lines and rule/world/fail labels, no code changes. Verified in jsdom.

title: Superposition animation: visibly show current + destination → result
description: Never silently replace one number with another. On each collision, visibly interact the two values: current Number + destination flow together and the resulting Number emerges. Fast enough not to impede play, clear enough to see causality (order of a few hundred ms). The point: make 'what happened to Number?' perceptually obvious, including whether it went UP.
acceptance_criteria: Each move shows the two operands interacting and the result emerging; animation does not block subsequent input.
close_reason: Destination tile glyph flies into the dot, result pops in with scale animation, delta indicator (↑ +n / ↓ n / — ±0 / ✕ invalid) rises, status number flashes up/down/flat. CSS-transition based, does not block input (verified rapid successive keypresses in jsdom).
